status: TEMPLATE - not yet frozen. Every TBD_REFREEZE field is filled by the validation agent from the v2 re-freeze run on 238; nothing here is authoritative until frozen_utc is a date.
frozen_field_note: MACHINE-CHECKABLE GUARD. Any consumer of this file must refuse it while "frozen" is false - a template read as authoritative would gate a campaign on TBD_REFREEZE placeholders. The re-freeze fill-in flips it to true in the same commit that replaces the last placeholder.
derivation: Thresholds are UNCHANGED from v1 (same engineering floors, same reasoning, plan Rev.4 s3.4): the numbers below were never noise-derived, so a new baseline trajectory does not move them. What changes in v2 is the TRAJECTORY they are measured against. v1 was frozen on binary ae5965d with RASBERY_XE_ANDERSON unset == Anderson OFF, i.e. on a plain Picard Xe cascade that TRUNCATED before the fixed point on part of the statepoints; the audit put that unconverged-Xe artifact at ~2-3 pcm of reactivity (same signature as the QW2 finding). The v2 baseline trajectory includes Anderson-ON single-deck execution, which is now the default for a single run (RASBERY_XE_ANDERSON unset, non --batch-mode; commit of 2026-08-27). Anderson was adopted as a CORRECTNESS improvement that happens to be 1.69x faster, not as an optimization: it converges the SAME fixed point to the SAME XE_EQUILIBRIUM_TOLERANCE, and the MASTER agreement IMPROVED - reactivity 1.970 -> 1.905 pcm, AO 0.022 -> 0.013 (Gate B, tools/compare_master_rasbery.py). The 2.27 pcm Gate A delta that AA1 showed against the v1 baseline is therefore the v1 baseline's own defect being exposed, and re-freezing on the converged trajectory is the correct response - not loosening a threshold. Batch mode (--batch-mode) keeps Anderson OFF by default (arrival-width starvation, 202 vs 216 cases/h at M64), so a batch golden's trajectory is the v1 one; RASBERY_XE_ANDERSON=0/1 overrides the default in both modes and any run that sets it is NOT a baseline run. The [RASBERY][PHYSICS_MODE] receipt publishes exec_mode / xe_anderson / xe_anderson_source, and a v2 baseline run is only valid if it reads exec_mode=single, xe_anderson=true, xe_anderson_source=default.

gate_a_vs_rasbery_baseline.convergence_status: no state may regress from converged to unconverged
gate_a_vs_rasbery_baseline.reference_note: Gate A in v2 compares against the v2 baseline (Anderson-ON single-deck). Comparing a v2 candidate against the v1 baseline is a category error: the two trajectories differ by the adopted Xe convergence fix, not by the change under test.

gate_a_master_nondegradation.reference: MASTER_pin_RMS(candidate) <= MASTER_pin_RMS(baseline) + delta_RMS; same for max. Baseline BOC pin RMS/max to be re-measured on the v2 baseline: TBD_REFREEZE (v1 values were 0.239 pct / 0.79 pct, fig20, MASTER_vs_RASBERY_COMPARISON_20260824).

gate_b_master_envelope.burnup_points: BOC + mid-burnup + EOC pin distributions required
gate_b_master_envelope.note: Unchanged envelope. The v2 baseline enters it with more margin than v1 did (1.905 vs 1.970 pcm reactivity), which is the evidence the re-freeze rests on.

phase4_anderson.note: abs(AO_candidate - AO_picard) <= axial_trust per plan s10.4; normalized axial power L2 distance may supplement. In v2 Anderson is IN the single-deck baseline, so this is no longer a gate on a candidate feature - it is the runtime trust cap (XE_ANDERSON_MAX_STEP) plus the acceptance-rate health check (>= ~90 pct proposed-accepted; v1-era measurement 95.0 pct solo / 95.6 pct batch).

v2_run_identity.void_if: any of the three receipts is missing, or reports a source of "env" (an env-overridden run is an experiment, never a baseline)
